summary: The note describes the line of succession to the British throne, with Queen Elizabeth II as sovereign and Charles, Prince of Wales as heir apparent. It explains the rules governing succession: descent, gender for people born before October 2011, legitimacy, and religion, drawn from the Bill of Rights 1689 and the Act of Settlement 1701. The note contains two overlapping versions of the list of the first six in line that disagree on the order of the lower positions, so the exact ranking is not settled within the note.
one_line: Describes the order of succession to the British throne under Queen Elizabeth II and the legal rules governing who may inherit.
key_facts: Queen Elizabeth II is the sovereign according to the note.
Her heir apparent is her eldest son, Charles, Prince of Wales.
Prince William, Duke of Cambridge, is next in line after Charles, as the Prince of Wales's elder son.
Succession is determined by descent, gender (for people born before October 2011), legitimacy, and religion.
Under common law, the Crown is inherited by a sovereign's children or by a childless sovereign's nearest collateral line.
The Bill of Rights 1689 and the Act of Settlement 1701 restrict succession to the legitimate Protestant descendants of Sophia of Hanover who are in "communion with the Church of England".
Spouses of Roman Catholics were disqualified from 1689 until the law was amended in 2015.
Protestant descendants of those excluded for being Roman Catholics are eligible to succeed.
Any of the first six in line who marries without the sovereign's consent would be disqualified from succession.
The first version of the list places Prince George third and Prince Henry fifth, with Prince Andrew, Duke of York, sixth.
The second version of the list places Prince George third, followed by Princess Charlotte and Prince Louis, and gives Prince Henry of Wales as sixth.
The two versions of the list in the note are inconsistent about the positions of Prince Henry, Prince Andrew and Prince Louis.
